_comment_family: The family name straight out of the file's name table (ID 1), and it
is safe to ask for by family alone here in a way Telegraf's is not:
Bebas Neue is one cut. There is no second weight sharing the name for
a request to land on by accident, so 'Bebas Neue' can only ever be
Bebas Neue has no lower case. Its lower-case codepoints are drawn as
capitals, which is worth knowing before reading a pack that sets it:
the capitals a Snapchat caption is set in are the face's own answer
and not a transformation laid over it.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes -
nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the Windows full name, then the
family. The family is included, unlike in the Telegraf packs, for the
reason given above: it names one cut here because there is only one,
so a machine answering to it is answering with these letterforms.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before anything is
drawn. Chosen all the same: Bebas Neue is a tall condensed display
face with no lower case, and Anton is the nearest thing in this app's
own fonts folder. Impact after it is the nearest thing Windows can be
